title: The gender dependence of postoperative pneumonia in women: A single-center study on gender dependence in thoracic surgical care
summary:
This study examines whether there are differences between women and men in the occurrence and course of pneumonia after chest surgeries. Postoperative pneumonias are among the most common complications following thoracic surgical procedures and can significantly worsen the healing process.
Using data from the years 2005 to 2025, all patients who developed pneumonia after a thoracic operation will be analyzed. It will be assessed whether the frequency, severity, or course of this complication differs between the sexes. Additionally, it will be investigated which risk factors, surgical procedures, and treatment measures are associated with an increased or decreased risk. The goal is to better understand possible gender-specific differences and further improve postoperative care.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients who developed postoperative pneumonia following thoracic surgical procedures between 2005 and 2025 with regard to gender-specific differences.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who were treated in thoracic surgery from 2005 to 2025 Postoperative pneumonia after thoracic surgical procedure
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who were treated in thoracic surgery before 2005 or after 2025
no postoperative pneumonia after thoracic surgical procedure
